sections.label: January 2026
sections.blurb: US forces captured Nicolás Maduro and the Monroe Doctrine came back into the vocabulary. India passed Japan to fourth place by nominal GDP, non-fossil capacity crossed half the installed total, the EU sent its first joint Republic Day chief guests, India took the BRICS chair, and the Supreme Court read menstrual health into Article 21.

sections.label: February 2026
sections.blurb: Sitharaman delivered her ninth budget against a 4.3% deficit target, Delhi hosted the AI Impact Summit, the US Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs, and Bangladesh voted for the first time since the Hasina uprising.

sections.label: March 2026
sections.blurb: The Supreme Court did more constitutional heavy lifting in one month than most years manage: a first-ever passive euthanasia order, a nine-judge bench on the meaning of 'industry', and an appellate mechanism grafted onto West Bengal's voter-roll revision. Parliament passed the Finance Bill and a contested transgender rights amendment in the same fortnight. Abroad, the Strait of Hormuz shut down mid-war, Nepal elected a 41-year-old mayor as prime minister, and India put an uncrewed capsule closer to a human spaceflight than it has ever been.

sections.label: April 2026
sections.blurb: Assembly elections in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Kerala, Assam and Puducherry ran alongside the Census 2026 rollout and the 131st Amendment Bill. Abroad, the Strait of Hormuz crisis kept oil and shipping in the headlines.

sections.label: May 2026
sections.blurb: The Iran war reached the Strait of Hormuz and the EU carbon border tax went live. At home the Cabinet cleared four more Supreme Court judges, the Court read emergency medical care into Article 21, Assam passed a uniform civil code, and the RBI handed the Centre ₹2.86 lakh crore.

sections.label: June 2026
sections.blurb: The Islamabad Memorandum ended the four-month 2026 Iran war on the same day France's G7 summit wrapped up at Evian, while at home the Supreme Court swore in five new judges and handed down an unusually dense run of rights-expanding rulings, from a footpath-based reading of Article 19 to a rupee value on a homemaker's unpaid labour. RBI held rates but cut its growth forecast, citing the war directly, and the Delimitation Bill stalled again in Parliament.

sections.label: July 2026
sections.blurb: The Iran war entered its fifth month, the Monsoon Session opened with the 130th Amendment Bill, and the Cabinet cleared ₹2.19 lakh crore for Semicon 2.0. Covers 1–25 July, and the passage bank stops at six.

sections.label: Polity & Constitution
sections.blurb: The permanent half of the paper. Articles, amendments, the bodies that enforce them and the cases that interpreted them, ranked by how often they actually appear.

sections.label: Landmark Judgments & Legal GK
sections.blurb: The constitutional canon plus the legal vocabulary the paper assumes you already have. Cases ranked by how often they actually appear.

sections.label: Modern Indian History
sections.blurb: From Plassey to Partition, ranked by exam frequency. Dates, sessions, pacts and the people who were actually in the room.

sections.label: World Organisations & Treaties
sections.blurb: Founding years, headquarters cities and current heads, plus the treaty calendar. The most mechanically examined material in the whole syllabus.

sections.label: Economy & Banking
sections.blurb: Central banking, the budget and the institutions that run Indian economic policy. Definitions first, because that is what the paper tests.

sections.label: Science, Space & Defence
sections.blurb: The space programme, the nuclear and missile programme, health vocabulary and the everyday physics and chemistry the paper asks about by name.

sections.label: Awards & Honours
sections.blurb: Civilian and gallantry honours in order of precedence, and the international prizes with the Indian winners the paper expects you to name.

sections.label: Geography & Environment
sections.blurb: Physical India, the monsoon, the protected-area network and the treaties that govern it. The treaty detail itself lives in World Organisations.

topics.title: US forces capture Maduro; the Monroe Doctrine returns
topics.hook: US forces raided Caracas on 3 January 2026 and flew President Nicolas Maduro to New York on narcoterrorism charges, and Washington's oldest claim on Latin America is back in play.

topics.title: EU's Costa and von der Leyen become Republic Day's first joint chief guests
topics.hook: For the first time in 77 years of Republic Day, the chief guests were not a country but the European Union, represented by two presidents, and the visit doubled as the 16th India-EU Summit.

topics.title: India takes over the BRICS chair for 2026
topics.hook: India became BRICS chair on 1 January 2026, its fourth turn at the helm, and this time it must steer a bloc of ten members instead of the original five.

topics.title: Supreme Court: no customs duty on electricity from SEZ to DTA
topics.hook: The Supreme Court ruled on 5 January 2026 that electricity generated inside a Special Economic Zone and sold outside it cannot be taxed as if it were an imported good.

topics.title: Supreme Court reads menstrual health into Article 21
topics.hook: The Supreme Court held that the right to life under Article 21 includes a right to menstrual health, pushing sanitary pad access and dignity for menstruating students into the language of fundamental rights.

topics.title: Padma Awards 2026: 131 honoured, Dharmendra and V.S. Achuthanandan among posthumous picks
topics.hook: The government named 131 Padma Award winners on the eve of Republic Day 2026, including five Padma Vibhushans, two of them awarded posthumously.

topics.title: Gaza ceasefire enters phase two as the last hostage body is recovered
topics.hook: The US declared phase two of its Gaza ceasefire plan on 16 January 2026, even as monitors counted over a thousand violations of the deal struck three months earlier.

topics.title: Russia, Ukraine and the US hold peace talks in Abu Dhabi
topics.hook: Ukrainian, Russian and American negotiators met in Abu Dhabi on 23-24 January 2026 for talks officials called '90 percent' of the way to a peace deal, with territory and a nuclear plant the last sticking points.

topics.title: RBI cuts the repo rate as growth outpaces inflation
topics.hook: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee cut the repo rate in its first meeting of 2026, choosing to back growth running near 8 percent over a hawkish stance on inflation that has already cooled sharply.

topics.title: China's live-fire drills push closer to Taiwan than ever
topics.hook: Chinese rockets landed within Taiwan's 24-nautical-mile contiguous zone during live-fire drills over the New Year, the closest Beijing has fired to the island since 2022.

topics.title: ISRO's first launch of 2026 fails to reach orbit
topics.hook: ISRO's PSLV-C62, carrying a DRDO earth-observation satellite and 15 co-passenger payloads, lifted off on 12 January 2026 but failed to reach orbit — a rare setback for India's most reliable launch vehicle.

topics.title: Davos 2026 convenes under 'A Spirit of Dialogue' as risk report flags misinformation
topics.hook: The World Economic Forum's 56th Annual Meeting ran in Davos from 19-23 January 2026, opening with a Global Risks Report that ranked misinformation the top short-term threat to the world for a second year running.

topics.title: Parliament's Budget Session 2026 convenes
topics.hook: Parliament's Budget Session opened on 28 January 2026, days before Nirmala Sitharaman's ninth straight Budget, which for the first time in Indian history fell on a Sunday.

topics.title: Khelo India Winter Games return to Leh with figure skating debut
topics.hook: The sixth Khelo India Winter Games opened in Leh on 20 January 2026, introducing Olympic figure skating to the domestic circuit for the first time.

topics.title: Supreme Court splits on Prevention of Corruption Act sanction requirement
topics.hook: A Supreme Court bench delivered a split verdict in January 2026 on whether prior government approval is constitutionally required before investigating a public servant for corruption.

topics.title: AM Green's Kakinada plant hits equipment milestone, signs Uniper deal
topics.hook: India's first mega green ammonia project, coming up at Kakinada, reached a major construction milestone in January 2026 and signed a long-term supply deal with Germany's Uniper.

topics.title: Bangladesh heads toward a February election amid strained India ties
topics.hook: With Bangladesh's general election set for February 2026, India-Bangladesh relations were unusually tense through January, unsettled by the fallout from Sheikh Hasina's 2024 ouster.

topics.title: Nepal's Gen Z-protest transition heads toward a March election
topics.hook: Months after Nepal's Gen Z protests toppled its government, former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli gave testimony to an inquiry probing the deadly crackdown, as the country moved toward March 2026 elections.

topics.title: Sudan's civil war deepens in Darfur
topics.hook: Civilian deaths and mass displacement kept mounting in Sudan's Darfur region through January 2026, as the Rapid Support Forces rejected a ceasefire proposal backed by the UN and African Union.

topics.title: Alcaraz completes the career Grand Slam at the Australian Open
topics.hook: Carlos Alcaraz beat Novak Djokovic in the 2026 Australian Open final to complete a career Grand Slam at 22, the youngest man to do so in the Open Era's recent history.

topics.title: Milan Cortina 2026 torch relay reaches Cortina, 70 years after 1956
topics.hook: The Olympic flame reached Cortina d'Ampezzo on 26 January 2026, seventy years after the town last hosted the Winter Games in 1956, ahead of the Milan-Cortina Games opening on 6 February.

topics.title: The Supreme Court tightens the 25% school quota
topics.hook: A private school that takes no state money still has to keep a quarter of its entry class for children it did not choose.

topics.title: Who may investigate a judge, and why none has ever been removed
topics.hook: The Constitution calls it removal, not impeachment, and in seventy-five years it has never been completed.

topics.title: India passes Japan to become the fourth largest economy
topics.hook: Fourth by the size of the pie and about one hundred and forty-first by the size of the slice.

topics.title: Non-fossil capacity passes half the installed total
topics.hook: India promised to get half its electricity capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030 and arrived early.

topics.title: The G4 propose a Council of twenty-six
topics.hook: Every proposal to expand the Security Council has to be approved by the five countries whose relative power it would reduce.

topics.title: Diego Garcia, the Chagos deal and the people who were removed
topics.hook: An advisory opinion said the islands should have gone with independence in 1968. The base is still there.

topics.title: India in the Arctic, and the sea route that is opening
topics.hook: A country with no Arctic coastline runs a research station there, because what happens on that ice decides the monsoon.

topics.title: The carbon credit scheme widens to 208 industries
topics.hook: A domestic carbon price is worth paying because somebody else will otherwise collect it at their border.

topics.title: Startup India at ten, and the IPO count
topics.hook: More new listings than any other country in the world, and most of the money raised went to companies nobody outside finance has heard of.

topics.title: Gig workers strike over the ten-minute delivery model
topics.hook: The law finally named them in 2020, and then did not bring the law into force.

topics.title: The Piprahwa relics come home
topics.hook: Gems buried with the Buddha, dug up by a colonial landowner in 1898, and auctioned in Hong Kong in 2025.

topics.title: Union Budget 2026-27: Sitharaman's ninth budget targets a 4.3% deficit
topics.hook: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented her ninth consecutive Union Budget on February 1, 2026, pushing capital spending up while trimming the fiscal deficit target to 4.3% of GDP.

topics.title: India AI Impact Summit 2026 and the New Delhi Declaration
topics.hook: India hosted the AI Impact Summit at Bharat Mandapam from February 16 to 21, 2026, and 92 countries and organisations signed the New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact.

topics.title: US Supreme Court strikes down Trump's IEEPA tariffs
topics.hook: On February 20, 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that the President cannot impose tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, unwinding Donald Trump's signature trade policy.

topics.title: Macron in Mumbai: India and France declare a 'Special Global Strategic Partnership'
topics.hook: President Emmanuel Macron's February 17-19 visit to India produced a 'Special Global Strategic Partnership', the highest tier France has offered any country, and launched the India-France Year of Innovation.

topics.title: BNP sweeps Bangladesh's first election since the Hasina uprising
topics.hook: Bangladesh voted on February 12, 2026 in its first general election since the 2024 uprising, and Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party won 209 of 299 seats, ending 20 years out of power.

topics.title: One month after Maduro's capture, Venezuela weighs an uncertain recovery
topics.hook: A month after a US military operation captured President Nicolas Maduro on January 3, 2026, CNN reported Venezuelans caught between eased sanctions and a wrecked economy, with acting president Delcy Rodriguez releasing political prisoners.

topics.title: Milano Cortina 2026: two Italian cities share the Winter Olympics
topics.hook: The Olympic Winter Games opened February 6, 2026 in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo, the first Winter Olympics officially hosted by two cities, running through February 22.

topics.title: Parliament passes the Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill, closing out the labour codes rollout
topics.hook: Both Houses passed the Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026 during the February leg of the Budget Session, confirming that three old labour laws stood repealed from November 21, 2025.

topics.title: Modi's Israel visit elevates ties to a 'Special Strategic Partnership'
topics.hook: Prime Minister Modi's February 25-26 state visit to Israel produced a 'Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation and Prosperity' and 16 agreements spanning AI, agriculture, and defence.

topics.title: Supreme Court finally takes up the CAA's constitutional challenge
topics.hook: Nearly two years after petitions were filed, the Supreme Court on February 19, 2026 began substantive hearings on the constitutionality of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, starting with pan-India objections before turning to Assam and Tripura-specific claims.

topics.title: India and China keep managing a cautious border thaw
topics.hook: Building on Wang Yi's 2025 visit, India and China moved through February 2026 to set up a general-level talks mechanism on their disputed boundary, even as Jaishankar insisted peace at the border remains a precondition for normal ties.

topics.title: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0: from policy to fabrication
topics.hook: The Budget cleared India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 at an overall outlay of Rs 1.25 lakh crore, up from Rs 76,000 crore for the first phase, shifting focus from capacity creation to deeper fabrication and design.

topics.title: Economic Survey 2025-26 and a rebased GDP series
topics.hook: Tabled a day before the Budget, the Economic Survey projected 7.4% growth for FY26, while a newly rebased GDP series with 2022-23 as the base year showed manufacturing growing fastest at 11.5%.

topics.title: RBI holds the repo rate at 5.25% for a second straight meeting
topics.hook: The Monetary Policy Committee, meeting February 4-6, 2026, unanimously kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25%, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra citing benign inflation and resilient growth.

topics.title: Gaza's ceasefire holds on paper as strikes continue
topics.hook: Despite a ceasefire in place since October 10, 2025, Israeli strikes killed at least 23 Palestinians in Gaza on February 4, 2026 alone, part of a pattern of continued violence through the month.

topics.title: India and the US strike an 18% tariff trade framework, then watch it wobble
topics.hook: India and the United States announced a trade framework on February 7, 2026 setting an 18% reciprocal tariff on Indian exports, only for the US Supreme Court to void its legal basis two weeks later.

topics.title: India joins the Pax Silica Coalition on chip supply chains
topics.hook: India joined the newly formed Pax Silica Coalition on February 20, 2026, alongside Australia, Israel, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, the UAE, the UK, and the US, to secure semiconductor and critical mineral supply chains.

topics.title: India and the Gulf Cooperation Council sign terms of reference for an FTA
topics.hook: India signed terms of reference with the Gulf Cooperation Council on February 5, 2026 to formally launch free trade agreement negotiations, building on $179 billion in bilateral trade for 2024-25.

topics.title: Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 gets a Rs 10,000 crore corpus
topics.hook: The Cabinet approved Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 on February 14, 2026 with a Rs 10,000 crore corpus, targeting high-tech, early-stage, and non-metro founders.

topics.title: Defence Acquisition Council clears Rs 3.6 lakh crore in procurement
topics.hook: The Defence Acquisition Council approved capital procurement worth Rs 3.6 lakh crore on February 12, 2026, spanning Rafale jets, T-72 tank upgrades, P-8I maritime aircraft, and a HAL-Safran missile joint venture.

topics.title: West Bengal's electoral roll revision reaches the Supreme Court
topics.hook: With 1.36 crore West Bengal voters flagged in questionable categories and 32 lakh unmapped, the Supreme Court extended deadlines and authorised Additional District Judges to hear claims before final rolls were published on February 28, 2026.

topics.title: Supreme Court revives a 9-judge bench to define 'industry'
topics.hook: On February 16, 2026, the Supreme Court revived a long-dormant reference to a nine-judge Constitution Bench to settle what counts as an 'industry' under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

topics.title: TERI's World Sustainable Development Summit marks its 25th edition
topics.hook: TERI's World Sustainable Development Summit ran February 25-27, 2026 in New Delhi for its Silver Jubilee edition, themed 'Transformations: Vision, Voices, and Values for Sustainable Development'.

topics.title: State of India's Environment 2026 warns seven planetary boundaries are breached
topics.hook: Released at the Anil Agarwal Dialogue on February 25, 2026, the Centre for Science and Environment's annual report found extreme weather struck India on 99% of days in 2025 and that seven of nine planetary boundaries have now been breached.

topics.title: India wins a record sixth U-19 Cricket World Cup
topics.hook: India beat England by 100 runs in Harare on February 7, 2026 to win the Under-19 Cricket World Cup for a record sixth time, with Vaibhav Suryavanshi scoring 175 off 80 balls.

topics.title: RCB defend their WPL title, beating Delhi Capitals
topics.hook: Royal Challengers Bangalore beat Delhi Capitals by 6 wickets on February 5, 2026 to win their second consecutive Women's Premier League title.

topics.title: Thailand holds a general election
topics.hook: Thailand elected all 500 members of its House of Representatives on February 8, 2026.

topics.title: Costa Rica holds general elections
topics.hook: Costa Rica held general elections on February 1, 2026, electing its President and Legislative Assembly.

topics.title: Damascus expands control as SDF integration begins
topics.hook: Syrian government forces entered the Kurdish-majority city of Qamishli on February 3, 2026 under a ceasefire and integration agreement absorbing the Syrian Democratic Forces into the state military.

topics.title: US-brokered Ukraine-Russia talks yield a prisoner swap in Abu Dhabi
topics.hook: Trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi concluded in early February 2026 with a 314-prisoner exchange and an agreement to resume military-to-military dialogue.

topics.title: National Science Day 2026 honours women in science
topics.hook: India observed National Science Day on February 28, 2026 with the theme 'Women in Science: Catalysing Viksit Bharat'.

topics.title: Bad Bunny wins Album of the Year at the 68th Grammy Awards
topics.hook: Bad Bunny's Spanish-language album won Album of the Year at the 68th Grammy Awards on February 1, 2026, a first for a primarily non-English record.

topics.title: Supreme Court orders sensitivity guidelines for POCSO trials
topics.hook: On February 10, 2026, the Supreme Court set aside a High Court's downgrading of a rape-attempt charge and directed the National Judicial Academy to draft sensitivity guidelines for POCSO trials.

topics.title: Supreme Court upholds a customs confession's admissibility in a 40-year-old case
topics.hook: Deciding a smuggling case pending for four decades, the Supreme Court on February 23, 2026 upheld that customs officers are not bound by the Evidence Act's restrictions on police confessions.

topics.title: NCERT withdraws a Class 8 chapter on judicial backlog after Supreme Court order
topics.hook: The Supreme Court on February 26, 2026 ordered the physical seizure and digital removal of a Class 8 NCERT chapter addressing judicial corruption and case backlog.

topics.title: RBI opens the door for banks to lend to REITs and InvITs
topics.hook: The RBI issued draft guidelines on February 13, 2026 letting commercial banks lend to listed REITs and InvITs for the first time, subject to a cap of 10% of eligible capital.

topics.title: Urban Challenge Fund gets a Rs 1 lakh crore commitment
topics.hook: The government committed Rs 1 lakh crore in central assistance through 2030-31 to the Urban Challenge Fund, targeting transit planning, water and sanitation, and climate resilience in cities.

topics.title: February 2026's notable deaths
topics.hook: February 2026 saw the deaths of Anand Sagar, son of filmmaker Ramanand Sagar, and veteran DD News reader Sarla Maheshwari, among other public figures.

topics.title: India and Malaysia deepen semiconductor and security ties
topics.hook: A February 7-8, 2026 India-Malaysia engagement covered semiconductors, vocational training, and national security cooperation.

topics.title: India and Brazil discuss rare earths and digital cooperation
topics.hook: A February 18-22, 2026 engagement with Brazil covered rare earth minerals, digital partnership, and MSME cooperation.

topics.title: Barbados holds elections for its House of Assembly
topics.hook: Barbados held elections for its House of Assembly on February 11, 2026.

topics.title: Draft rules tighten drug import oversight and offshore mineral tracking
topics.hook: February 2026 saw draft amendments to the Drugs Rules requiring manufacturer notification of product changes, alongside new Offshore Areas Mineral Rules mandating electronic vessel tracking.

topics.title: Supreme Court allows India's first court-ordered passive euthanasia
topics.hook: The Supreme Court let doctors at AIIMS Delhi withdraw life support from a man who had been in a vegetative state for twelve years, the first time a court itself ordered passive euthanasia rather than approving a family's plan.

topics.title: Nine-judge bench reserves verdict on what counts as an 'industry'
topics.hook: A nine-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant spent two days on a single word, 'industry', deciding whether a 1978 definition covering everything from hospitals to gurudwaras still holds.

topics.title: Supreme Court sets up 19 appellate tribunals for West Bengal's voter-roll revision
topics.hook: Facing complaints that lakhs of voters were struck off West Bengal's rolls without a proper hearing, the Supreme Court ordered the Election Commission to set up 19 appellate tribunals to hear their appeals before the state goes to the polls.

topics.title: Parliament passes the Transgender Persons Amendment Bill, dropping self-identification
topics.hook: Parliament amended the Transgender Persons Act, 2019 to remove the self-perceived gender identity that the Supreme Court had made a constitutional right in NALSA v Union of India in 2014, drawing condemnation from Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch.

topics.title: Finance Bill 2026 clears Parliament, closing the Budget Session
topics.hook: The Lok Sabha passed the Finance Bill 2026 by voice vote on 25 March, the last major step in giving legal effect to the Union Budget presented at the start of the Budget Session in January.

topics.title: Iran shuts the Strait of Hormuz; US launches strikes to reopen it
topics.hook: Iran mined and blocked the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes, prompting a US aerial campaign to reopen it and a Security Council resolution, co-sponsored by India, condemning Iranian attacks on Gulf states.

topics.title: Maduro's second US court appearance, and the Monroe Doctrine's return
topics.hook: Nicolas Maduro, abducted by US forces from Caracas in January, appeared in a US court for the second time on 26 March, insisting he remains a head of state and 'prisoner of war' rather than an ordinary criminal defendant.

topics.title: Le Pen's National Rally surges in French municipal elections, then falls short in the big cities
topics.hook: Marine Le Pen's National Rally won more than 60 municipalities in France's two-round municipal elections and posted historic scores, but failed to capture Marseille, Toulon, or Nimes, the big prizes it needed ahead of the 2027 presidential race.

topics.title: Nepal's Rastriya Swatantra Party wins a landslide; Balen Shah becomes PM at 35
topics.hook: Six months after Gen Z-led protests forced Nepal's prime minister to resign, voters handed a party formed only in 2022 a majority on its own, something no single party had managed in Nepal since 1999.

topics.title: Gaganyaan-1, ISRO's uncrewed test flight, targets its March launch window
topics.hook: ISRO pushed toward a March 2026 launch window for Gaganyaan-1, the first uncrewed test flight of India's human spaceflight programme, carrying the half-humanoid robot Vyommitra to rehearse the systems that will one day carry Indian astronauts.

topics.title: China's Two Sessions launch the 15th Five-Year Plan
topics.hook: China's National People's Congress opened its 2026 session on 5 March by approving the 15th Five-Year Plan and setting a GDP growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent, the country's slowest official target band in decades.

topics.title: The 11th Raisina Dialogue brings 110 countries to Delhi
topics.hook: India's flagship geopolitics conference drew around 2,700 participants from 110 countries to New Delhi, with Finland's President delivering the keynote under the theme 'Samskara: Assertion, Accommodation, Advancement'.

topics.title: Paris hosts the second World Nuclear Energy Summit
topics.hook: France and the IAEA co-hosted the second World Nuclear Energy Summit, where Belgium, Brazil, China, and Italy joined 38 other countries in endorsing a declaration to triple global nuclear capacity by 2050.

topics.title: Government declares India free of Left-Wing Extremism
topics.hook: Home Minister Amit Shah told the Lok Sabha that not a single district in India remains affected by Left-Wing Extremism, closing a chapter of insurgent violence that once ran through the 'Red Corridor' from central to southern India.

topics.title: President approves a wide reshuffle of state Governors
topics.hook: President Droupadi Murmu approved a sweeping reshuffle of Governors and Lieutenant Governors across multiple states in early March, including new appointments to West Bengal, Maharashtra, Telangana, Bihar, and Himachal Pradesh.

topics.title: Supreme Court orders a no-fault compensation policy for COVID vaccine deaths
topics.hook: The Supreme Court directed the Union government to frame a no-fault compensation policy for deaths that may have followed COVID-19 vaccination, while declining to legally attribute any specific death to the vaccine itself.

topics.title: Taranjit Singh Sandhu becomes Delhi's new Lieutenant Governor
topics.hook: Taranjit Singh Sandhu, India's former Ambassador to the United States, took charge as Delhi's Lieutenant Governor in mid-March, stepping into a post that repeatedly clashes with Delhi's elected government over who controls what.

topics.title: India beats New Zealand to win a third T20 World Cup title
topics.hook: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad to become the first team to win three T20 World Cup titles and the first host nation ever to win the tournament.

topics.title: India Climate Week and new 2035 emissions targets
topics.hook: India used the second India Climate Week to unveil interim 2035 climate targets, including a 47% cut in emissions intensity and 60% non-fossil power capacity, drawing criticism from environmental groups for lacking ambition.

topics.title: India and China hold border talks as China reasserts a Shaksgam Valley claim
topics.hook: India and China's Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination reviewed the border situation in March, even as China's earlier reassertion of a claim over the Shaksgam Valley kept tensions along the Line of Actual Control unresolved.

topics.title: Gaza's ceasefire holds, unevenly, through March
topics.hook: The internationally brokered Gaza ceasefire remained formally in place through March 2026, but Israel continued operations against Hamas and diplomats kept pushing for the group's disarmament, with Gaza's Government Media Office logging thousands of violations since the truce began.

topics.title: Russia's drone war intensifies as Ukraine fights to restore power
topics.hook: Russia launched more drones at Ukraine in March 2026 than in any earlier month of the war, even as Ukrainian forces intercepted 92% of them and worked to restore power capacity knocked out by earlier strikes on its energy grid.

topics.title: Bangladesh's newly elected Parliament convenes
topics.hook: Bangladesh's 13th National Parliament began its first session in March 2026, seating a Bangladesh Nationalist Party-led majority elected in February, a year and a half after Sheikh Hasina's government was toppled by student-led protests.

topics.title: GST collections cross ₹1.78 lakh crore as the cess winds down
topics.hook: March 2026 GST collections reached about ₹1.78 lakh crore, up 8.2% year-on-year, as the government completed the phase-out of the GST compensation cess first introduced in 2017.

topics.title: Dutch municipal elections test the post-Wilders political landscape
topics.hook: The Netherlands held municipal elections across 333 municipalities on 18 March 2026, a local-level gauge of how Dutch politics is realigning after Geert Wilders's Party for Freedom topped the 2023 general election.

topics.title: North Korea holds single-party elections to its Supreme People's Assembly
topics.hook: North Korea held elections on 15 March 2026 for its 15th Supreme People's Assembly, a ritual vote in which candidates run unopposed and turnout is officially reported near 100 percent.

topics.title: 'One Battle After Another' sweeps the 98th Academy Awards
topics.hook: Paul Thomas Anderson's 'One Battle After Another' won six Oscars including Best Picture and Best Director at the 98th Academy Awards, while Michael B. Jordan and Jessie Buckley took the lead acting honours.

topics.title: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
topics.hook: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman introduced a 107-clause bill amending the Companies Act, 2013 and the LLP Act, 2008, which Parliament then referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee rather than passing directly.

topics.title: PM Research Chair Scheme opens applications
topics.hook: The Ministry of Education opened applications for the Prime Minister Research Chair Scheme, designed to draw accomplished Indian-origin researchers abroad back into India's higher-education and research institutions.

topics.title: BCCI Naman Awards honour Gill, Mandhana, and cricket's veterans
topics.hook: The BCCI's Naman Awards in New Delhi handed Shubman Gill and Smriti Mandhana their best-international-cricketer honours, while Roger Binny and Rahul Dravid received the Board's lifetime achievement award named after India's first Test captain.

topics.title: Supreme Court: an unsigned charge order sheet doesn't invalidate a trial
topics.hook: The Supreme Court clarified that a judge's failure to sign the order sheet while framing criminal charges does not by itself invalidate the trial, so long as the accused was properly informed of the charges and suffered no real prejudice.

topics.title: Delhi launches the Atal Canteen subsidised food scheme
topics.hook: Delhi's government launched the Atal Canteen scheme, offering subsidised meals to the poor through government-run canteens across the capital, with a budget of ₹104 crore.

topics.title: India co-sponsors UNSC resolution condemning Iran's Gulf attacks
topics.hook: India was among more than 130 countries co-sponsoring a UN Security Council resolution condemning Iran's missile and drone attacks on Gulf Cooperation Council states and Jordan, while continuing its own trade relationship with Iran through Chabahar port.

topics.title: Nandini Chakravorty becomes West Bengal's first woman Chief Secretary
topics.hook: Nandini Chakravorty served as West Bengal's Chief Secretary from 1 January to 15 March 2026, the first woman to hold the post in the state's history.

topics.title: India moves to operationalise its compliance carbon market
topics.hook: India adopted regulations to operationalise the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, its domestic compliance carbon market, targeting rollout by mid-2026.

topics.title: International Women's Day 2026 observed under two competing themes
topics.hook: 8 March 2026 marked International Women's Day, observed globally under the UN theme 'Rights. Justice. Action. For ALL Women and Girls,' while the independent internationalwomensday.com campaign used 'Give To Gain.'

topics.title: India Week celebrates India-Sri Lanka ties in Colombo
topics.hook: India Week 2026 in Colombo marked a week-long cultural celebration of India-Sri Lanka relations, coming as Sri Lanka's cricket team also processed a disappointing exit from the T20 World Cup on home soil.

topics.title: Computer scientist Sir Tony Hoare dies at 92
topics.hook: Sir Tony Hoare, the British computer scientist who invented the Quicksort sorting algorithm and Hoare logic for verifying program correctness, died in March 2026 at the age of 92.

topics.title: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill falls one vote-share short of women's reservation
topics.hook: On 17 April 2026 the Lok Sabha voted 298 to 230 for a bill meant to fast-track women's reservation and expand the House to 850 seats, and the bill still failed, because a constitutional amendment needs two-thirds of members present and voting, not a simple majority.

topics.title: Tamil Nadu gets its first hung assembly, and a film star's party tops the poll
topics.hook: Tamil Nadu voted on 23 April 2026 with the highest turnout in its history, and for the first time since 1967 no single Dravidian bloc came out with a majority — a two-year-old party founded by actor Vijay finished on top with 108 seats, twelve short of the 118 needed to govern alone.

topics.title: West Bengal votes out Mamata Banerjee's fifteen-year government
topics.hook: West Bengal voted in two phases, on 23 and 29 April 2026, and the BJP won 206 of the state's 293 assembly seats, ending Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress government after fifteen unbroken years in power.

topics.title: Fifty-one countries meet on the Strait of Hormuz as the 2026 Iran war grinds on
topics.hook: France and the United Kingdom co-chaired a summit of 51 countries on 17 April 2026 to defend freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint carrying roughly a fifth of the world's traded oil, five weeks into a war that began when the US and Israel killed Iran's supreme leader.

topics.title: India's first caste census since 1931 begins counting 1.4 billion people
topics.hook: India's 16th decennial census began houselisting operations on 1 April 2026, over three million officials deployed, and for the first time since 1931 it is collecting caste data — a question the government dropped from every census after Independence.

topics.title: A nine-judge bench reopens Sabarimala, and religious freedom for everyone with it
topics.hook: A nine-judge Supreme Court bench began sixteen days of hearings on 7 April 2026 to review the 2018 Sabarimala judgment, reopening not just the question of women's temple entry but the broader test courts use to decide which religious practices the Constitution actually protects.

topics.title: Kalpakkam's breeder reactor goes critical, and India enters stage two of a 1954 plan
topics.hook: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam attained first criticality at 8:25 pm on 6 April 2026, making India only the second country after Russia to operate a fast breeder reactor at this scale, and opening the door to the thorium-fuelled third stage of a nuclear programme first sketched by Homi Bhabha in 1954.

topics.title: Three months after Maduro's capture, Chevron signs a deal in Caracas
topics.hook: On 13 April 2026, Chevron signed an agreement with Venezuela's interim government at Miraflores Palace, three months after a US military operation captured President Nicolás Maduro, a chapter in the two-century pattern of American intervention that began with the Monroe Doctrine of 1823.

topics.title: Orban's sixteen years end as Hungary elects Peter Magyar
topics.hook: Viktor Orban conceded defeat on 12 April 2026 after Peter Magyar's Tisza Party won 138 of 199 seats in Hungary's parliament, ending sixteen years of Orban's rule and a governing style Brussels had long treated as a European Union outlier.

topics.title: Amaravati becomes Andhra Pradesh's sole capital, a decade-old question finally closed
topics.hook: Parliament passed the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 on 1-2 April, giving Amaravati statutory and retrospective status as Andhra Pradesh's sole and permanent capital, closing a capital-city dispute that has run since the state split from Telangana in 2014.

topics.title: RBI holds the repo rate at 5.25% as a war it didn't start reshapes its options
topics.hook: The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee met from 6 to 8 April 2026 and unanimously left the repo rate unchanged at 5.25%, judging that a supply-side shock from the West Asia conflict called for watching rather than reacting.

topics.title: India slips to sixth-largest economy on the IMF's April table, without actually getting poorer
topics.hook: The IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook ranks India sixth by nominal GDP, behind the US, China, Germany, Japan and the UK, a fall from earlier fourth-place projections driven not by weaker growth but by a weaker rupee and a technical statistical revision.

topics.title: BJP wins a third Assam term as Kerala swings back to Congress
topics.hook: Assam, Kerala and Puducherry voted in a single phase on 9 April 2026, with Assam recording 84.4% turnout as the BJP secured a third straight term on its own strength, while Kerala's Left Democratic Front lost to the Congress-led United Democratic Front.

topics.title: India switches on a 1,000 km quantum-secure communication line
topics.hook: India's Department of Science and Technology announced on 8 April 2026 a fully indigenous, 1,000-kilometre secure quantum communication network built by the startup QNu Labs under the National Quantum Mission, a step toward encryption that classical computers, and future quantum ones, cannot break by brute force.

topics.title: Parliament decriminalises another batch of minor offences under Jan Vishwas 2.0
topics.hook: Parliament passed the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 in early April, extending a decriminalisation drive that began in 2023 by converting more minor regulatory offences from criminal penalties into civil fines.

topics.title: Odisha lays the foundation for India's first 3D glass chip packaging plant
topics.hook: Odisha broke ground on 19 April 2026 for India's first Advanced Glass Semiconductor Packaging Unit in Bhubaneswar, a ₹1,943 crore facility using glass substrates, not silicon, to stack chips for AI and defence electronics.

topics.title: Three April rulings, three different limits on state power
topics.hook: Three separate April 2026 Supreme Court rulings, on dismissing a policeman without inquiry, on whether cooperative milk unions count as 'State,' and on a mandatory step in criminal trials, each narrowed how far an authority can act without giving someone a chance to answer first.

topics.title: CSE's State of India's Environment 2026 flags floods, heat and a monitoring gap
topics.hook: The Centre for Science and Environment's annual State of India's Environment report, published in April 2026, warns that flood risk is rising with climate change even as gaps persist in India's air-pollution monitoring network, in a report series that has run since 1982.

topics.title: Two housekeeping bills, a shared paramilitary command and a faster bankruptcy process
topics.hook: Parliament passed the Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill in early April 2026, tidying up how paramilitary forces are administered and how stressed companies are resolved.

topics.title: IPL 2026 resumes its second phase across 12 cities
topics.hook: The BCCI's second-phase IPL 2026 schedule, 50 matches across 12 venues from 13 April to 24 May, resumed on 13 April with Sunrisers Hyderabad hosting Rajasthan Royals, days after a fixture swap forced by Ahmedabad's municipal elections.

topics.title: India's envoy calls on Bangladesh's new PM as ties reset post-Hasina
topics.hook: India's High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Pranay Verma, paid a courtesy call on Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on 6 April 2026, part of a cautious diplomatic reset after the political upheaval that removed Sheikh Hasina from power.

topics.title: Myanmar's junta chief wins an indirect presidential vote he engineered
topics.hook: Myanmar held an indirect presidential election on 3 April 2026, five years after the 2021 military coup, and Min Aung Hlaing, the general who led that coup, won the presidency through a process his own military-appointed electoral college controlled.

topics.title: Asha Bhosle, voice of seven decades of Hindi cinema, dies at 92
topics.hook: Playback singer Asha Bhosle died on 12 April 2026 in Mumbai at 92, after recording an estimated 12,000 songs across multiple Indian languages over a career spanning roughly seven decades.

topics.title: EU leaders meet informally as Hungary's exit from the Orban era reshapes the bloc
topics.hook: European Union heads of state met informally on 23-24 April 2026 under European Council President Antonio Costa, days after Hungary's election result removed the bloc's most persistent internal veto-wielder from office.

topics.title: PM Mudra Yojana turns 11, still India's biggest small-loan scheme
topics.hook: The Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana marked 11 years since its April 2015 launch, continuing to provide collateral-free loans of up to ₹20 lakh to small and micro entrepreneurs who fall outside conventional bank lending.

topics.title: Ladakh keeps pushing for Sixth Schedule status, and Delhi keeps promising talks
topics.hook: Activist Sonam Wangchuk, released in March after six months in detention, told reporters on 7 April 2026 that Ladakh's demands for statehood and Sixth Schedule protections needed 'open-minded and sincere' talks, ahead of Union Home Minister Amit Shah's scheduled 30 April visit.

topics.title: Delhi launches Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana for girl children
topics.hook: The Delhi government launched the Lakhpati Bitiya Yojana on 2 April 2026, a savings-linked scheme aimed at securing a lump-sum payout for girls born into the state's lower-income households once they reach adulthood.

topics.title: RoSCTL scheme extended for textile exporters amid global uncertainty
topics.hook: The Ministry of Textiles extended the RoSCTL scheme on 3 April 2026, continuing tax and duty rebates for textile and apparel exporters as global trade uncertainty from the West Asia conflict weighed on shipping costs.

topics.title: C.D. Gopinath, India's oldest living Test cricketer, dies at 96
topics.hook: C.D. Gopinath, who had held the distinction of being India's oldest living Test cricketer, died on 10 April 2026 at the age of 96.

topics.title: Mohsina Kidwai, veteran Congress leader, dies at 94
topics.hook: Mohsina Kidwai, a veteran Congress leader and former Union Minister who held several central cabinet portfolios across decades, died on 8 April 2026 at the age of 94.

topics.title: Bulgaria's Progressive Bulgaria wins a low-turnout legislative election
topics.hook: Bulgaria held a legislative election on 19 April 2026, with Progressive Bulgaria winning the largest seat share on a turnout of just 49.3 percent.

topics.title: Maldives holds local council elections with record turnout
topics.hook: The Maldives held its fifth local council elections on 4 April 2026, recording a record 73 percent turnout for a local-level vote.

topics.title: Peru's Popular Force tops a fragmented legislative election
topics.hook: Peru held a legislative election on 12 April 2026, with Popular Force winning the largest seat share ahead of Together for Peru, on 73.8 percent turnout.

topics.title: Women's Prize for Fiction and Non-Fiction announce 2026 shortlists
topics.hook: The Women's Prize for Fiction and the Women's Prize for Non-Fiction announced their 2026 shortlists on 22 April 2026, continuing a British literary award founded in 1996 to counter the historical under-representation of women on major book-prize lists.

topics.title: UAE intercepts 19 missiles and 26 drones as Iran widens its strikes
topics.hook: Iran struck the United Arab Emirates directly in early April 2026, and the UAE's air defences intercepted 19 ballistic missiles and 26 drones in a single wave, a sign the 2026 Iran war had widened beyond its original combatants.

topics.title: India clears a second S-400 squadron deal with Russia
topics.hook: India's Defence Acquisition Council approved buying five additional S-400 Triumf air defence squadrons from Russia, building on an earlier $1.1 billion deal for 288 missiles cleared after the 2025 Pakistan conflict, with deliveries expected between late 2028 and early 2029.

topics.title: India approves $8.7 billion in precision-strike weapons from Israel
topics.hook: India approved an $8.7 billion acquisition of Israeli precision-strike weaponry, including SPICE-1000 smart munition kits and long-range missiles, one of the largest single defence deals in India-Israel military cooperation.

topics.title: India's archers and volleyball team post rare international results
topics.hook: India won 16 medals, including seven gold, at the World Archery Para Series in Bangkok in early April 2026, where teenage quadruple-amputee archer Payal Nag beat world number one Sheetal Devi to win the compound women's final.

topics.title: Stranded 23 days in the Hormuz standoff, an Indian tanker finally docks
topics.hook: The Indian-flagged tanker Jag Vasant docked in Mumbai carrying an LPG cargo in early April 2026, after being stranded 23 days in the Strait of Hormuz amid the standoff over shipping access during the 2026 Iran war.

topics.title: India expands the RELIEF scheme as West Asia tensions squeeze exporters
topics.hook: India expanded the RELIEF scheme on 18 April 2026 to support exporters facing disrupted shipping and higher freight costs from the ongoing West Asia conflict.

topics.title: CJI Surya Kant presides over a packed April docket
topics.hook: Justice Surya Kant, the 53rd Chief Justice of India since 24 November 2025, presided in April 2026 over both the nine-judge Sabarimala bench and the Court's regular docket, ahead of a tenure ending 9 February 2027.

topics.title: The Iran war reaches the Strait of Hormuz
topics.hook: In May 2026 the war that began with the killing of Iran's Supreme Leader in February spread into the Strait of Hormuz, and the world found out again how one narrow waterway can move the price of everything.

topics.title: The Supreme Court upholds the Bihar electoral roll purge
topics.hook: On 27 May 2026 the Supreme Court closed the book on the Bihar Special Intensive Revision, ruling that striking 47 lakh names off the rolls before an election was lawful, proportionate and within the Election Commission's power.

topics.title: No fundamental right to bet: the Supreme Court upholds the rummy and poker ban
topics.hook: The Supreme Court ruled on 27 May 2026 that Tamil Nadu and Karnataka can ban online rummy and poker played for money, holding that betting on a game of skill is still gambling, and gambling gets no protection under the right to trade.

topics.title: India signs 10-year long-term agreement for Chabahar Port operation
topics.hook: India Global Ports Limited (IPGL) signed a 10-year contract with Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation to equip and operate the Shahid Beheshti Terminal at Chabahar Port.

topics.title: The Supreme Court goes from 34 judges to 38
topics.hook: The Constitution never fixed the number. Parliament has raised it seven times, and the pendency argument has been the same each time.

topics.title: Emergency medical care read into Article 21
topics.hook: A hospital that turns away a road accident victim for want of paperwork is now refusing a fundamental right, not just breaching an ethical rule.

topics.title: Assam passes a Uniform Civil Code Bill
topics.hook: Article 44 tells the state to endeavour. It says nothing about which state.

topics.title: The RBI transfers ₹2.86 lakh crore to the Centre
topics.hook: A central bank does not have shareholders, so what it hands the government every August is not really a dividend, and the size of it is decided by a formula almost nobody reads.

topics.title: India takes the IORA chair and hosts the Indian Ocean Dialogue
topics.hook: Twenty-three countries around one ocean, and the only rule for joining is a coastline on it.

topics.title: The EU carbon border tax goes live and India objects
topics.hook: A tariff that calls itself a climate measure, on goods that were never made in Europe.

topics.title: India and Vietnam move to the top tier of partnership
topics.hook: India has about thirty strategic partnerships. Only a handful sit at the top of the ladder, and the rungs mean something.

topics.title: India-UAE trade crosses $100 billion
topics.hook: A trade agreement negotiated in eighty-eight days, and the target it set for 2030 was met four years early.

topics.title: The essential religious practices doctrine comes back up
topics.hook: A court that decides which parts of a religion are essential is doing theology, and it has been doing it since 1954.

topics.title: Q4 growth at 7.2% and the unemployment number beside it
topics.hook: Two numbers released within days of each other, measured by two different offices, and only one of them is easy to argue about.

topics.title: The GST Council cuts rates on EV batteries and medical devices
topics.hook: The one constitutional body where the Centre holds a third of the votes and can still be outvoted, in theory.

topics.title: The Asiatic lion count reaches 891
topics.hook: Every Asiatic lion alive is descended from a population that dropped to perhaps twenty animals in one forest in Gujarat.

topics.title: DRDO tests a glide weapon and an Agni-5 variant
topics.hook: A missile that splits into several warheads on separate paths is one weapon on paper and several problems for an interceptor.

topics.title: RCB take a second consecutive IPL title
topics.hook: A franchise that lost three finals in seventeen years has now won two in a row.

topics.title: Cristian Mungiu wins a second Palme d'Or
topics.hook: Only ten directors have won the Palme d'Or twice, and the tenth did it nineteen years after the first.

topics.title: World Migration Report 2026: India leads on diaspora and remittances
topics.hook: The largest flow of money into India from abroad is not investment. It is people sending money home.

topics.title: Deep-sea mining and the authority nobody wants to obey
topics.hook: The seabed beyond national jurisdiction is legally the common heritage of mankind, which is a strong phrase with a weak enforcement mechanism.

topics.title: The Global Forest Goals Report counts the loss
topics.hook: The world agreed in 2015 to increase forest area. Ten years on, forty million hectares had gone the other way.

topics.title: The Islamabad Memorandum ends the 2026 Iran war
topics.hook: On 17 June 2026 the US and Iran signed the Islamabad Memorandum, ending nearly four months of war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a crisis with a direct line to India's oil bill.

topics.title: Supreme Court finds a Fundamental Right to Walk on footpaths
topics.hook: In Maniyar Iliyaz v. P. Ayyappan, the Supreme Court read a fundamental right to walk safely on a demarcated footpath into Article 19(1)(d), the freedom to move freely — a ruling built for a footpath-encroachment fact pattern that any city student recognises.

topics.title: Five new judges take oath at the Supreme Court, including its second woman elevated from the Bar
topics.hook: On 2 June 2026, five new judges — Sheel Nagu, Shree Chandrashekhar, Sanjeev Sachdeva, Arun Palli and V. Mohana — were sworn in to the Supreme Court, with Justice Mohana only the second judge elevated directly from the Bar to the top court.

topics.title: RBI holds rates, cuts growth forecast and moves to shore up the rupee
topics.hook: The RBI's June 2026 Monetary Policy Committee kept the repo rate at 5.25%, cut its FY27 growth forecast to 6.6% and raised its inflation forecast to 5.1%, then rolled out a rupee-support package explicitly citing the West Asia war.

topics.title: G7 leaders meet at Evian for the first time in 23 years
topics.hook: France hosted the G7 summit at Evian from 15 to 17 June 2026 — the group's return to the same lakeside town 23 years after it last met there — producing joint statements on growth, critical minerals and child safety online, and providing the backdrop for the Islamabad Memorandum signing.

topics.title: Delimitation Bill, 2026 fails to pass, government looks to the monsoon session
topics.hook: The Delimitation Bill and its companion constitutional amendment, introduced in April to redraw Lok Sabha seats using the 2011 Census and expand the House to 850 members, failed to secure the numbers in the budget session and is now being pushed to the monsoon session.

topics.title: Supreme Court declares rehabilitation a fundamental right for trafficking survivors
topics.hook: In Prajwala v. Union of India, the Supreme Court held that rehabilitation of trafficking survivors is not a discretionary welfare measure but a fundamental right, and ordered a comprehensive, victim-centred protection plan.

topics.title: Lt Gen Dhiraj Seth named the next Chief of the Army Staff
topics.hook: Lieutenant General Dhiraj Seth, then Vice Chief of the Army Staff, was named the next Chief of the Army Staff, effective 30 June 2026 — a straightforward vertical succession that is still worth knowing cold for GK.

topics.title: Supreme Court prices a homemaker's unpaid work into accident compensation
topics.hook: In Shishu Pal v. Surjeet, the Supreme Court created a new head of compensation, 'Loss of Domestic Care', valuing a homemaker's unpaid household labour at Rs 30,000 a month when calculating motor-accident death claims.

topics.title: India and Pakistan clash again over the Indus Waters Treaty
topics.hook: Pakistan's defence minister said in June 2026 that Pakistan would go to war if it judged its water security genuinely threatened by India's handling of the Indus Waters Treaty — rhetoric that stopped short of action but kept a 1960 treaty back in the headlines.

topics.title: The first 48-team FIFA World Cup kicks off across three countries
topics.hook: The 2026 FIFA World Cup opened on 11 June with Mexico's match at Estadio Azteca, the first edition of the tournament expanded to 48 teams and the first jointly hosted by three countries — the United States, Mexico and Canada.

topics.title: Supreme Court issues draft rules for AI use inside courtrooms
topics.hook: The Supreme Court issued draft Regulations for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Courts, 2026, on 3 June, days after separately warning that judges relying on AI-generated fake citations could face misconduct proceedings.

topics.title: India hosts the 11th BRICS Foreign Policy Dialogue as 2026 chair
topics.hook: India's Ministry of External Affairs hosted the 11th BRICS Foreign Policy Dialogue in New Delhi on 5 June 2026, part of its year-long turn as BRICS chair, bringing together policy-planning heads from the grouping's expanded membership.

topics.title: China steps up maritime patrols near Taiwan after a Japan-Philippines defence deal
topics.hook: China launched a special maritime enforcement operation east of Taiwan in June 2026, responding to a new Japan-Philippines agreement to negotiate maritime borders and deepen defence cooperation.

topics.title: Draft amendments would cut the poorest households' free foodgrain quota
topics.hook: Draft amendments to the National Food Security Act, floated on 23 June 2026, would change how much subsidised grain the poorest Antyodaya Anna Yojana households get — from 35 kg per household per month to 7 kg per person, a formula that helps large families but can cut allocation for small ones.

topics.title: Neelkanth Mishra named India's Executive Director at the World Bank
topics.hook: Economist Neelkanth Mishra was appointed India's Executive Director at the World Bank on 4 June 2026, representing India, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Sri Lanka on the institution's board.

topics.title: Lokhande Prashant Sitaram named CBSE chairperson
topics.hook: The government named Lokhande Prashant Sitaram as the new Chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education on 2 June 2026.

topics.title: World Environment Day 2026 held in Baku, Azerbaijan
topics.hook: Azerbaijan hosted the global observance of World Environment Day 2026 on 5 June, with the day's theme centred on climate change and the country running a national campaign titled 'Inspired by Nature. For Climate. For Our Future.'

topics.title: Cabinet approves a Rs 10,000-crore fuel stabilisation fund for Indian airlines
topics.hook: On 3 June 2026, the Union Cabinet approved a Rs 10,000-crore fund to cushion Indian airlines against fuel-price volatility caused by the West Asia crisis.

topics.title: South Korea holds nationwide local elections
topics.hook: South Korea held its 2026 local elections on 3 June, choosing all 17 metropolitan mayors and provincial governors along with hundreds of municipal mayors and council seats in a single nationwide vote.

topics.title: Pakistan-administered Kashmir sees its deadliest unrest in years
topics.hook: Nearly two weeks of protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir left at least 24 people dead in June 2026, the region's deadliest unrest in years, prompting road closures, an internet shutdown and media restrictions.

topics.title: Thailand's 2026 general election results are finalised
topics.hook: Results of Thailand's 2026 general election were finalised in mid-2026, the latest chapter in a political cycle that has repeatedly swung between elected governments and military-backed intervention since the 2014 coup.

topics.title: India's economy grew 7.7% in FY 2025-26
topics.hook: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation put India's GDP growth at 7.7% for the financial year 2025-26, a figure RBI then used as the base against which it forecast a slower 6.6% for the following year.

topics.title: RBI bars dark patterns in banking and shifts fraud liability to banks
topics.hook: Through June 2026, RBI issued two consumer-facing rules in quick succession: banning dark patterns and compulsory bundling in banking products on 15 June, then shifting the liability burden for fraudulent transactions onto banks on 24 June.

topics.title: Foreign Contribution Regulation Rules tightened for NGOs
topics.hook: Amended Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rules notified on 22 June 2026 prescribe approved purposes for foreign donations and require NGOs to utilise at least 75% of a previous instalment before drawing the next one.

topics.title: Israel accused of breaching the US-brokered Lebanon ceasefire
topics.hook: Even as the Islamabad Memorandum formally ended the wider 2026 Iran war, Israeli strikes on Lebanon after 17 June were reported as violations of the same US-brokered agreement Israel's own government had just been party to.

topics.title: Cabinet approves Small Hydro Power Development Scheme, 2026-31
topics.hook: The Union Cabinet approved the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme for FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31, with an outlay of Rs 2,584.60 crore to install small hydro capacity.

topics.title: Government eases tax and outbound-investment rules for foreign capital
topics.hook: Two June 2026 notifications loosened rules around foreign capital: an income-tax ordinance exempted FIIs and the Bank for International Settlements from tax on government-securities interest and gains, while amended FEMA rules expanded outbound investment eligibility for individuals.

topics.title: Uttarakhand holds its first round of municipal elections
topics.hook: Uttarakhand's municipal elections were held on 9 June 2026, with results declared two days later, filling seats across three of the state's municipalities.

topics.title: India accuses Pakistan of 'officially sponsored disinformation' at the UN
topics.hook: India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Harish Parvathaneni, accused Pakistan of officially sponsored misinformation at a UN Security Council session on Afghanistan, after Pakistan referred to groups inside its own borders using the term 'Fitna al-Hindustan.'

topics.title: Notable Indian deaths in June 2026
topics.hook: June 2026 saw the deaths of Tamil filmmaker Bharathiraja and Odia writer Jagannath Prasad Das, two figures whose work shaped their respective regional cultural traditions.

topics.title: Supreme Court reaffirms Article 329(b) bars courts from interfering mid-election
topics.hook: In Meenakshi Natarajan v. Election Commission of India, the Supreme Court reaffirmed that Article 329(b) expressly bars judicial interference in electoral matters while an election process is ongoing.

topics.title: Supreme Court orders coordinated crackdown on illegal sand mining in the Chambal Sanctuary
topics.hook: Acting suo motu, the Supreme Court ordered a coordinated surveillance and prosecution framework to stop illegal sand mining threatening endangered aquatic wildlife in the National Chambal Sanctuary.

topics.title: DISHA legal-aid scheme extended through 2030-31
topics.hook: The government extended the DISHA scheme, which funds legal-services infrastructure, through FY 2030-31 with an allocation of Rs 255 crore.

topics.title: First high-level China-Taiwan meeting since 2016
topics.hook: A high-level meeting between a mainland Chinese official and Xi Jinping specifically on cross-strait matters, the first such meeting since 2016, signalled Beijing's attempt to look conciliatory to Taiwanese voters ahead of the island's November 2026 local elections.

topics.title: New York and Colorado hold 2026 state primary elections
topics.hook: New York held its state primary on 23 June 2026 and Colorado on 30 June, early markers in the run-up to that year's US midterm elections.

topics.title: Coal Exchange Rules notified to launch electronic coal trading
topics.hook: The government notified Coal Exchange Rules on 4 June 2026, operationalising an electronic trading platform for coal.

topics.title: Supreme Court: arbitration clauses don't oust consumer forum jurisdiction
topics.hook: In T.K.A. Padmanabhan v. Abhiyan Coop. Group Housing Society, the Supreme Court held that consumer remedies are statutory and independent, so an arbitration clause in a contract cannot eliminate a consumer's right to approach a consumer forum.

topics.title: The Iran war grinds into its fifth month
topics.hook: The US and Israel have been bombing Iran on and off since 28 February 2026, and by late July neither side has stopped — an exam favourite because it touches nuclear non-proliferation, oil chokepoints, and the limits of the UN Security Council.

topics.title: Monsoon Session opens with the 130th Amendment Bill back in play
topics.hook: Parliament's Monsoon Session (20 July-13 August) reopened the fight over the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, which would force a Prime Minister, Chief Minister, or minister out of office after 30 days in judicial custody — a direct test of the balance between accountability and the presumption of innocence.

topics.title: RBI holds the repo rate and cuts its growth forecast
topics.hook: The Reserve Bank of India held its repo rate at 5.25% in June's policy review but cut its FY27 growth forecast to 6.6% and raised its inflation forecast to 5.1%, citing war-driven oil prices and a weak rupee — the kind of decision CLAT likes to test through numbers, not adjectives.

topics.title: Cabinet clears ₹2.19 lakh crore for Semicon 2.0 and mobile manufacturing
topics.hook: The Union Cabinet approved a ₹2.19 lakh crore package on 15 July covering Semicon 2.0, a new Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme, and a National Investment Policy for Urea — the kind of scheme cluster CLAT likes to test through crore figures and ministry names.

topics.title: A bill to raise the Supreme Court's strength from 33 to 37 judges
topics.hook: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, listed for the Monsoon Session, would raise the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges — excluding the Chief Justice — from 33 to 37, the latest in a series of expansions meant to chip away at pendency.

topics.title: India holds the BRICS chair through a year of global turbulence
topics.hook: India took over the BRICS chairmanship on 1 January 2026 and is building toward hosting the summit in New Delhi in September — its fourth time chairing the bloc — with an energy ministers' meeting in Gurugram in June already testing the year's theme, 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability.'

topics.title: Spain wins the first 48-team World Cup
topics.hook: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup final on 19 July, becoming the first men's champion of the tournament's new 48-team format and the first nation to hold both the men's and women's World Cup titles at once.

topics.title: Supreme Court confronts AI-hallucinated case law
topics.hook: On 2 July, the Supreme Court set aside an NCLT order built on fabricated, AI-generated legal citations — a ruling that puts India alongside a small but growing list of jurisdictions confronting what happens when lawyers or tribunals use generative AI without checking whether the cases it cites actually exist.

topics.title: One regulator to replace UGC, AICTE, and NCTE
topics.hook: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025, which merges the UGC, AICTE, and NCTE into a single higher-education regulator, is before a Joint Parliamentary Committee and listed for the Monsoon Session 2026 — a structural reform CLAT could test through which body did what before the merger.

topics.title: NATO meets in Ankara as Turkey hosts for the first time since 2004
topics.hook: NATO's 32 members met in Ankara on 7-8 July 2026, Turkey's first NATO summit since Istanbul in 2004, with Secretary General Mark Rutte pressing allies on defence spending and continued support for Ukraine even as protests outside the venue were banned for nearly two weeks.

topics.title: Trafficking survivors get a constitutional right to rehabilitation
topics.hook: In Prajwala v. Union of India, the Supreme Court read a constitutional right to rehabilitation into Articles 21 and 23 for trafficking survivors, ordering India's first comprehensive Victim Protection Plan with mandatory compliance deadlines — a ruling still shaping government response through July 2026.

topics.title: India joins the WTO's Fisheries Subsidies Agreement
topics.hook: India deposited its Instrument of Acceptance for the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies on 20 July 2026, becoming the 123rd member to join a deal that bans subsidies fuelling illegal fishing and the depletion of already-overfished stocks — a rare case of a trade agreement built entirely around an environmental goal.

topics.title: Supreme Court calls degrading bail conditions 'abhorrent'
topics.hook: A bench led by CJI Surya Kant struck down bail conditions that required accused persons to perform degrading tasks like cleaning police stations, calling such conditions 'abhorrent' and 'unknown to law' — a ruling that ties bail jurisprudence firmly to Article 21's dignity guarantee.

topics.title: Anurag Jain named NITI Aayog CEO
topics.hook: The government appointed senior IAS officer Anurag Jain as NITI Aayog's new CEO for a two-year term on 22 July, keeping the post — always held by a serving or retired bureaucrat, never an elected figure — in career-civil-servant hands as it has been since the body's creation.

topics.title: A cluster of top bureaucratic and diplomatic postings
topics.hook: Within the first week of July, the Centre extended Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri's tenure by a year, reappointed Ravi Agrawal as CBDT Chairman till December 2026, named new chiefs at BPR&D, NCRB, and SVPNPA, and posted Sanjeev Jain as India's Ambassador to North Korea.

topics.title: Opposition pushes a privilege motion over Operation Sindoor casualty figures
topics.hook: Congress plans to move a privilege motion against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in the Monsoon Session, accusing him of misleading Parliament about troop casualties during Operation Sindoor, India's earlier military response in its conflict cycle with Pakistan.

topics.title: India takes 'AI for All' to the UN's first AI governance dialogue
topics.hook: India's delegation, led by Union Minister of State Kirti Vardhan Singh, attended the inaugural UN Global Dialogue on Artificial Intelligence Governance in Geneva on 6-7 July, pitching India's 'AI for All' framework of inclusive, human-centric AI development against tighter regulatory models elsewhere.

topics.title: Gaganyaan's crew module clears key qualification tests
topics.hook: ISRO completed three major qualification tests on the crew module for Gaganyaan, India's first crewed spaceflight programme, in July 2026 — progress on the ground even as the crewed launch itself remains not yet scheduled.

topics.title: FCRA amendment softens penalties, tightens oversight
topics.hook: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 cuts the maximum jail term for FCRA lapses from five years to one, while adding an oversight framework for what happens to an organisation's assets when its FCRA registration lapses.

topics.title: Jannik Sinner defends his Wimbledon title
topics.hook: Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev in a five-set Wimbledon final to win his second consecutive title and fifth Grand Slam overall, joining a short list of Open Era men to defend a Wimbledon crown.

topics.title: Bangladesh's measles epidemic reaches a legal reckoning
topics.hook: A measles outbreak in Bangladesh had killed 738 people by 5 July 2026, prompting a legal complaint against interim government chief Muhammad Yunus and three health officials over their handling of the epidemic.

topics.title: Supreme Court sets up an expert panel to protect the Aravallis
topics.hook: The Supreme Court constituted a five-member expert committee in July 2026 to scientifically define ecological zone boundaries in the Aravalli Hills, aiming to stop mining and construction from further eating into one of India's oldest mountain ranges.

topics.title: Cabinet clears a ₹3,030 crore scheme for the chemicals sector
topics.hook: The Union Cabinet approved a ₹3,030 crore scheme for India's chemicals sector on 24 July, the final piece of a fortnight of manufacturing-focused approvals that also covered semiconductors, mobile phones, and urea.

topics.title: India unveils its first native turbojet engine
topics.hook: India unveiled its first indigenously developed turbojet engine in the 350 kg thrust category on 22 July 2026, a small but symbolically loaded step in a country that has struggled for decades to build its own jet engines despite building its own aircraft.

topics.title: Ladakh's Puga Valley gets India's deepest geothermal wells
topics.hook: India commissioned its deepest geothermal wells at Puga Valley, Ladakh, in July 2026, tapping a site long known for hot springs and sulphur deposits to advance a renewable-energy source India has been slow to develop compared to solar and wind.

topics.title: TribeX launches to digitise tribal arts and knowledge
topics.hook: Union Minister Jual Oram launched TribeX, a digital learning platform for tribal arts, culture, and traditional knowledge, at a national workshop in Bhubaneswar in July 2026 — part of a wider pattern of India digitising cultural and skill-development programmes for specific communities.

topics.title: IAF Rafales join Exercise Pitch Black in Australia
topics.hook: The Indian Air Force sent Rafale fighter jets to Australia for the multinational exercise Pitch Black 2026, deepening India-Australia defence cooperation under the same broad Quad-adjacent framework that has driven joint exercises across the Indo-Pacific.

topics.title: The World Public Summit holds its first African edition
topics.hook: Addis Ababa hosted the inaugural African edition of the World Public Summit on 29-30 July 2026, under the theme 'New World: Africa in Shaping a Shared Future,' with sessions on Pan-African economic integration and ethical AI.

topics.title: A deadly prison riot rocks Negombo, Sri Lanka
topics.hook: A clash between rival drug gangs inside a prison in Negombo, Sri Lanka, killed 27 people, including four prison officers, in one of the deadliest single incidents in the country's overcrowded prison system in recent years.

topics.title: Cricket loses Sir Garfield Sobers
topics.hook: Sir Garfield Sobers, widely regarded as the greatest all-rounder in cricket history, died on 17 July 2026 at 89 — a West Indian great whose 365 not out stood as the highest individual Test score for 36 years.

topics.title: Indian civilian and gallantry honours
topics.hook: Four civilian awards in order, three gallantry awards in wartime and three in peacetime, and one constitutional rule about how none of them may be used.

topics.title: International prizes and the Indians who have won them
topics.hook: Six Nobel categories, one that is not technically a Nobel, and a short list of Indian winners that gets asked in full.

topics.title: Sports: trophies, tournaments and which sport they belong to
topics.hook: Twenty trophy names, each attached to exactly one sport, and a handful of tournament facts that recur every year.

topics.title: The Nobel Prizes: five from a will, one from a central bank
topics.hook: The man who invented dynamite read his own obituary, did not like it, and left his fortune to a set of prizes.

topics.title: Cinema, literature and the arts: the awards and who gives them
topics.hook: Which body confers which award, and the small list of firsts that keeps appearing.

topics.title: Days, observances and the themes that go with them
topics.hook: A date on the calendar is the cheapest question a paper can ask, and the cheapest mark to lose.

topics.title: The Reserve Bank, the Monetary Policy Committee and the rates that matter
topics.hook: One bank, six rates, a six-member committee and an inflation target written into law in 2016.

topics.title: The Union Budget: the deficits, the funds and the constitutional articles
topics.hook: Three deficits that are easy to confuse, three government funds that are easier to confuse, and one date that moved in 2017.

topics.title: Taxation: direct, indirect, and how GST rearranged everything
topics.hook: One tax replaced seventeen, needed a constitutional amendment to exist, and is run by a council where the Centre alone cannot pass anything.

topics.title: Measuring the economy: GDP, inflation and the indices that rank India
topics.hook: Six measures of national income, two measures of inflation, and about a dozen international indices whose publisher is the question.

topics.title: The banking system: nationalisation, bad loans and the regulators
topics.hook: Fourteen banks nationalised in one night in 1969, a bankruptcy code in 2016 that finally let lenders take a company away from its promoter, and four regulators who keep colliding.

topics.title: The external sector: balance of payments, reserves and trade rules
topics.hook: A current account that runs a deficit, a capital account that funds it, and a set of trade rules India argues with every year at Geneva.

topics.title: From the Planning Commission to NITI Aayog
topics.hook: A body with no constitutional or statutory basis directed India's investment for sixty-five years, and was abolished by a press release.

topics.title: Physical India: the six divisions, the monsoon and the coordinates
topics.hook: A country that spans 30 degrees of latitude, sets its clocks by a line through Mirzapur, and gets three quarters of its rain in four months.

topics.title: Protected areas and the law that creates them
topics.hook: Four categories of protected area, one Act from 1972 with six schedules, and a tiger count that is quoted every four years.

topics.title: The river systems and how the water is divided
topics.hook: Three rivers rise within a hundred kilometres of one another near Mansarovar and end up in three different countries.

topics.title: World geography: the lines, the extremes and the chokepoints
topics.hook: A hundred and twenty miles of dredged channel decides the freight cost of half of Europe.

topics.title: The Ghats, the hotspot and the reports nobody adopted
topics.hook: A 1,600 km ridge older than the Himalayas, listed as one of the world's eight hottest biodiversity hotspots, still without an agreed conservation boundary.

topics.title: Soils, crops and where the food actually comes from
topics.hook: Two soil types cover more than half the country, and they support entirely different crops for entirely different reasons.

topics.title: Ranges, peaks and the passes that carry the traffic
topics.hook: A pass is where a border becomes negotiable, which is why so many of them have been fought over.

topics.title: Plates, earthquakes and the zones the building code uses
topics.hook: India is still moving north into Asia at about five centimetres a year, and the Himalayas are the receipt.

topics.title: The monsoon machinery: El Nino, the dipole and the cyclone seasons
